preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line) <= 50000 for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and int(line) <= 50000)
preconditions.description: The first line of input is T (1 ≤ T ≤ 50000), the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(n_line) <= 500000 for n_line in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and 'n' in line.lower()])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line is n (1 ≤ n ≤ 500000), the number of vertices in the tree.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 for n, edges in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+n-1]]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: Each test case has exactly n-1 edges, forming a tree.

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= int(v) <= n and 1 <= int(u) <= n for v, u in [line.split() for line in edges]) for n, edges in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[i+1:i+1+n-1]]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: Each edge connects vertices v and u where 1 ≤ v, u ≤ n.

preconditions.expression: all(len(colors) == n for n, colors in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), stdin.splitlines()[i+n]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: The last line of each test case is a string of length n, where each character is 'W' or 'N'.

preconditions.expression: all(any(c == 'N' for c in colors) for n, colors in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), stdin.splitlines()[i+n]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: There is at least one uncolored vertex ('N') in each test case.

preconditions.expression: all(not any(all(c == 'W' for c in path) for path in get_all_paths(tree, n) if len(path) == 3) for n, colors in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i]), stdin.splitlines()[i+n]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)])
preconditions.description: No path of three white vertices ('W') exists initially in any test case.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line in ['White', 'Draw', 'Black'] for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'White', 'Draw', or 'Black', indicating the game result with optimal play.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line == 'White') == (white_wins(tree, colors, n)) for tree, colors, n, stdout_line in zip(get_trees(stdin), get_colors(stdin), get_n_values(stdin), stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output is 'White' if and only if the white player can force a win with optimal play, given the initial tree and coloring.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line == 'Black') == (not white_wins(tree, colors, n) and black_wins(tree, colors, n)) for tree, colors, n, stdout_line in zip(get_trees(stdin), get_colors(stdin), get_n_values(stdin), stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output is 'Black' if and only if the black player can force a win with optimal play, given that white cannot force a win.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line == 'Draw') == (not white_wins(tree, colors, n) and not black_wins(tree, colors, n)) for tree, colors, n, stdout_line in zip(get_trees(stdin), get_colors(stdin), get_n_values(stdin), stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output is 'Draw' if neither player can force a win with optimal play.
